title: Make sense of years and calendars

lessons.objective: Separate the weekday cycle from month and year lengths.
Put years into boxes of one hundred.
Find out why February sometimes gets an extra day.
Discover how a date jumped forward while life went on as usual.

sources.name: US Naval Observatory — The 21st century and 3rd millennium
NASA Space Place — What Is a Leap Year?
UK legislation — Calendar (New Style) Act 1750, sections 1–2
Royal Museums Greenwich — Leap years and the 1752 calendar change

glossary.definition: A group of one hundred years.
The extra day, 29 February, added in a leap year.
A system for giving dates to days, months and years.

outcomes: Distinguish a seven-day week from a calendar month.
Place a positive CE year in its century.
Distinguish a calendar date change from elapsed time.
description: Centuries, leap years and eleven missing days: untangle the oddities of our calendar, one short read at a time.
introduction: Start with a week and a month. Then zoom out to centuries, test the rules for leap years and discover why a real calendar once skipped eleven date labels.
prerequisites: No previous history reading required. The century examples use positive CE years.
